solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drug supplier's quick to limit damage

indicators.note: to limit something is to hem it in, so the word for quick closes around the word for damage

parts.note: pacy means fast or quick
harm means damage

explanation.surface: A spokesman insists the drug company acted fast to contain the harm done.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Drug supplier' stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist's shop is where medicines are dispensed, so it is a supplier of drugs.

clue.text: Revolutionary measure imposed on school

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: put, as in put on someone, can mean imposed

explanation.surface: A radical policy is forced on a school.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden attempt to overthrow a government by force is a revolutionary act.

clue.text: Road leading one to ancient place

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the letter for one heads the word for place

parts.note: a means one
a venue is a place where things happen, here one where something old is held

explanation.surface: A road that takes you to some old ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ancient' adds only colour to the place; the letters come from A and VENUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad, often tree-lined street is a kind of road.

clue.text: Deformed young woman almost slept with writer

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for slept with is dropped

parts.note: to have had someone is slang for having slept with them
a pen is something that writes

explanation.surface: A scandal: a disfigured girl nearly had an affair with an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims HAD to HA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something twisted out of its proper shape is deformed or malformed.

clue.text: Irrational cops could be intriguing

indicators.note: could be signals that these letters may be rearranged to form something else

explanation.surface: Police officers acting without logic might make for a gripping story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intriguing' looks like 'fascinating', but it means plotting.
explanation.definitionFit: Intriguing in the sense of scheming or plotting secretly describes the behaviour of a plotter.

clue.text: Flight case damaged wings of plane

indicators.note: damaged means knocked out of shape, so the letters of the word case are rearranged
the wings of a word are its outside letters, here its first and last

explanation.surface: Baggage-hall trouble: a suitcase got broken, and the aircraft's wings too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges CASE into ESCA; 'wings of' plane gives PE.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight in the sense of fleeing danger is a getaway, a breaking free.

clue.text: Character in Greek tragedy's first to leave in disgrace

indicators.note: to leave means to go away, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: a stigma is a mark of disgrace

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A figure in a Greek tragedy must depart in shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' of tragedy is T, which 'to leave' removes from STIGMA.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, the Greek equivalent of S, is a character in that script.

clue.text: University employee of no real use

definitions.meaning: a lecturer or researcher at a university
a question that is only theoretical, with no practical bearing, is said to be this

explanation.surface: A sneer that a university lecturer is useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A university lecturer is a scholar; a purely theoretical point has no practical relevance.

clue.text: Denounce what senior management get paid?

parts.note: an exec, short for executive, is a senior manager
the rate is the amount a person gets paid

explanation.surface: An invitation to condemn the size of bosses' pay.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags reading the answer as two words: an executive's pay rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to curse or condemn loudly, to denounce.

clue.text: Poorly understood development of strip mine put off following review

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the reversed piece comes after the anagram
the development of something reshapes it, so the letters of strip mine are rearranged
a review looks back, so the word for put off is read backwards

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage

explanation.surface: A planning objection to an open-cast mine was misread after a review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development of' turns STRIP MINE into MISINTERP; 'review' turns DETER into RETED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wrongly read or misunderstood has been taken the wrong way.

clue.text: Corrupt senator is betraying country

indicators.note: corrupt means twisted out of its proper form, so the letters of senator are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crooked politician is accused of selling out the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' looks like an adjective describing the senator, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The crime of betraying one's own country, by aiding its enemies, is the legal offence named here.

clue.text: Person with no appreciation of what it costs to throw game

indicators.note: to throw is to muddle or disorder, so the card game's letters are shuffled

parts.note: gin is gin rummy, a card game
the rate for something is the price it costs

explanation.surface: Someone ungrateful who knows exactly how much it costs to rig a match.
explanation.walkthrough: An indirect anagram: 'throw' acts on a synonym for game (the card game gin), not on the clue's own word, giving ING.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungrateful person, one who shows no thanks for kindness received, is called this.

clue.text: Symptom of toxic gas that makes me sick?

parts.note: CO is the chemical formula for carbon monoxide, a poisonous gas
ugh is the exclamation of disgust, said of something sickening

explanation.surface: Breathing poison fumes produces a sign of illness, as the sufferer groans.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacking spasm of the chest is a common sign of colds and lung illness.

clue.text: Sailor and soldier meeting head of state

indicators.note: meeting means joining up with, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a private is the lowest-ranking soldier
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the Queen and so the British head of state

explanation.surface: A seaman and an infantryman are presented to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is crossword shorthand for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A licensed pirate, or a crewman of such an armed private ship, is a kind of seafarer.

clue.text: Psychic hints about controlling lives following ceremony

indicators.note: controlling means holding in check, so the reversed word encloses the next pieces
about here means turned around, so the word for hints is read backwards

parts.note: tips are hints or pieces of advice

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the word for lives goes after the word for ceremony

parts.note: a ritual is a ceremony
is, as in 'he is', can mean exists or lives

explanation.surface: A medium offers clues about running people's lives after some ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the hints into SPIT; 'lives' must be read as the verb (he is, i.e. exists), not the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who claims contact with the dead is a medium, a person said to have psychic powers.

clue.text: Activist upset about anarchist leader reverting to old behaviour

indicators.note: about means around, so the anagram goes round the single letter
upset means overturned, so the letters of activist are reordered
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A campaigner annoyed by an anarchist chief who is backsliding into old ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges ACTIVIST into TAVISTIC, and 'about' puts it around the A from 'anarchist leader'.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwback traits that reappear from ancestors are said to be this, reversion to a primitive type.

clue.text: Children's worrying, dishonest behaviour

parts.note: CH is an abbreviation for children; the 's stands for is
eating, as in what's eating you, means worrying or troubling

explanation.surface: The children's anxious, deceitful conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worrying' looks like an adjective, but it means troubling, as in 'what's eating him?'
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking the rules to gain an advantage, or being unfaithful, is dishonest conduct.

clue.text: Forward author's study about turning up on time

parts.note: the author's, ie the writer is, gives I'm

indicators.note: about turning means facing the other way, so the word up is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a den is a study or private room

explanation.surface: A pushy writer's study is concerned with turning up punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'author' is the setter speaking of the setter, and the 's means 'is'. The turned word comes before the study despite the clue's order; in a down clue 'on time' puts T below.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward in the sense of cheeky or presumptuous describes someone rude or insolent.

clue.text: I'm not sure article changing sides in Italian is particularly helpful

parts.note: hum is a noise of hesitation or doubt
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the sides are left and right, so an L becomes an R in the word Italian

explanation.surface: A doubtful remark that a news item about a grammatical change in Italian is very useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing sides in' Italian swaps its L (left) for R (right), giving ITARIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable aid that relieves suffering is especially helpful to people in need.

clue.text: Keyboard ready to accept authentication code

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the word for ready encloses the code

parts.note: set means ready, as in ready, steady, go
a PIN, personal identification number, verifies identity

explanation.surface: A computer keyboard waits for a password to be typed.
explanation.definitionFit: A small harpsichord-like instrument played from keys is an old keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Los Angeles Police Department is under pressure still

indicators.note: in a down clue, the pieces that follow go below the letter for pressure

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police forces

explanation.surface: The Los Angeles police are under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface spells out LAPD, but the department is Britain's CID, the detective branch. In a down clue 'is under pressure' puts P on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Still water is calm, unruffled and tranquil.

clue.text: Person who's 16 is more grown up about coming back

parts.note: adult can be treated as an adjective with comparative adulter, more grown up

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone aged sixteen claims to be more mature on the way home.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 points to 16-down, the clue for dishonest behaviour; the surface reads it as an age. 'coming back' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unfaithful to a spouse is guilty of marital deceit, the behaviour 16-down names.

clue.text: Fool allowed to not finish book

parts.note: tit is British slang for a fool

indicators.note: to not finish means to stop short, so the last letter of the word for allowed is dropped

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: An idiot is permitted to leave a book unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: TIT is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: In publishing, a single book or publication is referred to by its name, a usage common in trade catalogues.

clue.text: Force that is left to protect politician

indicators.note: to protect means to surround and shield, so the first piece holds the politician

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Security for an elected official is drawn from the left.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive or compel someone to act is to force them.

clue.text: I retain run-down property that stops me moving?

indicators.note: run-down means dilapidated, so the letters of I retain are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: An owner keeps a dilapidated house that ties them down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'property' reads like real estate, but it is a physical property; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, a body's resistance to changes in motion is a property; in people, it is sluggishness.

clue.text: Wasn't it an iceberg partially responsible for this?

indicators.note: partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question: surely an iceberg played a part in this disaster?
explanation.definitionFit: The great liner famously sank in 1912 after striking an iceberg, so the ice was to blame for its loss.

clue.text: Learn that woman has returned ticket in advance

indicators.note: in advance means ahead, so the reversed ticket goes in front
returned means sent back, so the word for ticket is read backwards

parts.note: a tag is a label or ticket
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: Someone finds out a woman sent her ticket back early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns TAG into GAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather that something is so is to infer or find it out, to learn it.

clue.text: Learned about due date after bothering nurses

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the anagram cradles the short word for about
bothering means agitating, so the letters of due date are stirred into a new order

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: An expectant mother, fretting about her due date, is looked after by medical staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bothering' turns DUE DATE into EDUATED; 'nurses' puts C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone schooled and well read is learned, having had a good education.
